title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 89-91): M is a family of closed 'pieces' (multiplicités) with a partial order ≪ ('is a closed sub-piece of'). Each X ∈ M has a boundary ∂X and a 'shadow' Omb(X), the down-set of pieces ≪ X. Y|Z (or Y_Z) is the induced intersection of Y with Z. Y ∥ Z means Y_Z = ∅ (disjointness). Ỹ (or Y̌) is the set of faces/sub-pieces of Y. Grothendieck defines the 'interior' of X as a set of pieces: X° = {Y ∈ Omb(X) : Y ∥ ∂X}, the closed pieces of X missing its boundary. Notation: Y ∘≪ X means Y ≪ X and Y is not ≪ ∂X; Y ∘∘≪ X means Y ∈ X°.

Lemma 2 (assuming the auxiliary lemmas L1, L2, L3). Let Y ≪ X.
(a) Y ∘≪ X ⇔ Y° ⊂ X°.
(b) Y ∈ X° ⇔ for all Y' ∈ Ỹ, Y'° ⊂ X°.

This page proves (a) and the easy half of (b).

Proof of (a), ⇒. Take Y' ∈ Y°, so Y' ≪ Y ≪ X and Y' ∥ ∂Y. By transitivity of induction (restricting in X, then in Y), Y'_{∂X} = Y'|(Y_{∂X}). The hypothesis Y ∘≪ X gives Y_{∂X} ≤ ∂Y: the part of Y on ∂X lies in ∂Y, a 'properness' condition. Hence Y'|Y_{∂X} ≤ Y'|∂Y = ∅, so Y' ∈ X°.

Proof of (a), ⇐. Assume Y° ⊂ X°; we must show Y is not ≪ ∂X. This uses Y° ≠ ∅, boxed on the page, which he derives from L1 together with a 'divisibility axiom'. Take Z ∈ Y°; then Z ∈ X°, so Z ∥ ∂X. If Y ≪ ∂X, then Z ≪ ∂X, hence Z ∥ Z, which is absurd for a nonempty piece.

Proof of (b), ⇒. If Y ∈ X°, then Omb(Y) ⊂ X°, because X° is down-closed under ≪ ('comme on avait déjà noté'). Since Y'° ⊂ Omb(Y') ⊂ Omb(Y) ⊂ X°, this direction is trivial. The ⇐ direction is done on p. 91: if some Z ∈ Ỹ had Z ≪ ∂X, the hypothesis Z° ⊂ X° plus (a) would give Z ∘≪ X, a contradiction.

Purpose. This is part of an axiomatic, purely order-theoretic 'analysis situs' (Grothendieck's programme of tame/combinatorial topology from Esquisse §5). The aim is to recover open cells (interiors) and their disjointness relations from a poset of closed pieces with boundary, in order to prove the Lemma 1 criterion: X ∥ Y iff all interiors of faces are disjoint.
errors: The transcription line 'prouvons Y ≪ X, i.e. Y ≪ ∂X' must mean 'prouvons Y ∘≪ X, i.e. Y ≪̸ ∂X'. As written it is contradictory; the argument by contradiction only makes sense with the negation.

In (a) ⇒, the step Y_{∂X} ≤ ∂Y is attributed to the hypothesis Y ∘≪ X. If ∘≪ merely means 'Y ≪ X and Y not ≪ ∂X', this needs an axiom (purity/properness of the stratification). Otherwise it fails in general settings, e.g. a sub-piece touching ∂X at an interior point of itself. The dependence is not made explicit on this page.
The converse in (a) uses Y° ≠ ∅ and the fact that a piece is not disjoint from itself (nonemptiness). These are flagged as depending on L1 and a divisibility axiom, but are not proved here.

ideas.what: Interior of a closed piece defined as the down-set of sub-pieces disjoint from the boundary, X° = {Y ≪ X : Y ∥ ∂X}
ideas.modern_name: open cell / interior in an axiomatic face poset; pointless (locale-like) description of interiors
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in CW-poset / regular cell complex theory (Björner 1984 et al.); stratified spaces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches tame topology but not this formalism

ideas.what: Lemma: for Y ≪ X, Y meets the interior (is not in ∂X) iff Y° ⊂ X°, using the properness condition Y ∩ ∂X ⊂ ∂Y
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom stratification theory (frontier condition); folklore for cell complexes

ideas.what: Characterization Y ∈ X° iff all face-interiors of Y lie in X°
ideas.modern_name: closure/star decomposition: closed cell = union of open faces

missed.claim: The notes are part of an attempt to axiomatize 'analysis situs' purely in terms of a poset of closed pieces with boundary, induction (restriction) and disjointness, with explicit axioms (divisibility, L1-L3). Interiors and transversality are recovered order-theoretically. This axiomatic tame-topology framework was never published or completed.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible point of comparison with o-minimal / tame geometry and with combinatorial (exit-path, poset-stratified) approaches. But the content on this page is elementary lemma-checking and not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification lemmas inside an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology framework. The framework itself has documentary interest, but this page contains no new result or unexpected connection.
transcription_corrections: '[-Supposons-] Y°⊂X° prouvons Y≪X, i.e. Y≪∂X' should read 'Supposons Y°⊂X°, prouvons Y ∘≪ X, i.e. Y ≪̸ ∂X'.
'Je jamais [?] [-...-] n'ai [?] pas utilisé ici' is probably 'Je n'ai jamais [pas] utilisé ici …' or similar.
'Ah Dieu [?], absurde' is probably 'Ah bon, absurde' or simply 'absurde'.
'∀Y'∈Y̌, Y'°⊂X°': the check mark denotes the face set Ỹ, consistent with p. 89/91.
'Y'°⊂Omb(Y') [?] ⊂ X°' is consistent with the image.
